ur-nigin.draftGloss: Ur-nigin (Langdon Ur-nigin) — first king of the fourth dynasty of Uruk, father of Ur-gigir; UR + the sign Langdon reads nigin, drawn on the copy as a pointed head joined to a box of horizontals rather than the plain LAGAB box, so the identification is uncertain; ur 'man, servant'; the sense of the name is not clear

ur-gigir.draftGloss: Ur-gigir (Langdon Ur-gigir) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty), son of Ur-nigin; UR + GIGIR (LAGAB×BAD, 'chariot'), the second sign drawn wide on the copy, so its identification is Langdon's and uncertain; ur 'man, servant'; the sense of the name is not clear

kud-da.draftGloss: Kudda (Langdon Kudda) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty); written with two signs, taken here as TAR (read kud) + DA; the identification of the first sign is uncertain

šu-i₃-li₂.draftGloss: Shu-ili (Langdon Gimil-ili) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty); ŠU (Langdon's Gimil, drawn on the copy in a long form whose identification is his and uncertain) + NI-NI, read i₃-li₂, Akkadian ilī 'my god'

ur-{d}utu.draftGloss: Ur-Utu (Langdon Ur-ᵈBabbar) — king of Uruk (fourth dynasty); ur 'man, servant' + the sun-god Utu (the UD sign with the divine determinative; Langdon's Babbar): 'servant of Utu'

ugnim.draftGloss: army, troops; Langdon 'horde(s)' — written with three signs taken (after Langdon's reading ugnim) as KI.KAL.BAD; the copy draws three separate signs, a pointed sign like KI, a box with horizontals and a box with a crossing, and the identification of the last two is uncertain

gu-tu-um.draftGloss: Gutium (Langdon Gu-tu-um, 'Gutûm') — the land of the Gutians, a people of the eastern mountains whose 'horde' holds the kingship after Uruk; GU-TU-UM, once with the place-determinative KI; on this prism a further sign (a cluster of corner-wedges joined to a box of horizontals) stands between TU and UM in both VII 26 and VII 27; it is not identified and is shown as x; other copies have Gu-ti-um

tuk.draftGloss: to have, possess (the TUK sign); nu-tuk 'did not have'

im-ta-a.draftGloss: Imta (Langdon Im-ta-a, 'Imtâ') — the first named king of the Gutian horde; IM-TA-A; Legrain No. 1 has Im-bi-a, and Langdon thinks one of the two similar signs (TA, BI) a scribe's error

in-ki-šu₂.draftGloss: Inkishu (Langdon In-ki-šù) — a Gutian king; IN-KI + a small sign that Langdon reads šù, taken as ŠU₂; the identification of the last sign is his; a variant has gi for ki

ni-kil-la-gab.draftGloss: Nikillagab (Langdon Ni-kil-la-gab) — a Gutian king; NI + a plain box (LAGAB, given Langdon's value kil) + LA + GAB (the DU₈ sign); the value kil is Langdon's; the sense of the name is not clear

šul-me-e.draftGloss: Shulme (Langdon Šul-me-e, 'Šulmê') — a Gutian king; DUN (read šul) + ME + E

-meš.draftGloss: -meš — plural marker (written ME.EŠ; Akkadian scribal usage), here after a single king's name, where its sense is unclear (Langdon takes it as part of the name, 'Elulumeš')

i-ni-ma-ba-ki-eš.draftGloss: Inimabakesh (Langdon I-ni-ma-ba-ki-eš, 'Inimabakêš') — a Gutian king; I-NI-MA-BA-KI-EŠ

i-gi-eš-a-uš.draftGloss: Igeshaush (Langdon I-gi-eš-a-uš, 'Igêšauš') — a Gutian king; I-GI-EŠ-A-UŠ

ia-ar-la-gab.draftGloss: Yarlagab (Langdon I̯a-ar-la-gab, 'Jarlagab') — a Gutian king; IA (i̯a, consonantal y) + AR + LA + GAB (the DU₈ sign); Legrain No. 1 has Warlagaba, as the third king

i-ba-te.draftGloss: Ibate (Langdon I-ba-te) — a Gutian king; I-BA-TE

ia-ar-la.draftGloss: Yarla (Langdon I̯a-ar-la, 'Jarla(gaš)') — a Gutian king; IA-AR-LA, perhaps a shortened writing of a longer name (Langdon: probably Yarlagash)

ku-ru-um.draftGloss: Kurum (Langdon Ku-ru-um) — a Gutian king; KU-RU-UM

[…]-ne-di-in.draftGloss: […]-nedin (Langdon '…. ne-di-in') — a Gutian king; only the end of the name survives, NE-DI-IN, and the rest is lost

[…]-ra-bu-um.draftGloss: […]-rabum (Langdon '…. ra-bu-um') — a Gutian king; only the end of the name survives, RA-BU-UM, and the rest is lost

i-ra-ru-um.draftGloss: Irarum (Langdon I-ra-ru-um) — a Gutian king; I-RA-RU-UM

ib-ra-nu-um.draftGloss: Ibranum (Langdon Ib-ra-nu-um) — a Gutian king; IB-RA-NU-UM

ḫa-ab-lum.draftGloss: Hablum (Langdon Ḫa-ab-lum) — a Gutian king, father of Shu-Suen; ḪA-AB-LUM

ia-ar-la-ga-an-da.draftGloss: Yarlaganda (Langdon [I̯a-]ar-la-ga-an-da, 'Jarlaganda') — a Gutian king; IA-AR-LA-GA-AN-DA, the first sign in a break, restored by Langdon

ti-ri-ga.draftGloss: Tiriga (Langdon [Ti-ri-]ga) — the last Gutian king, who reigned forty days; TI-RI-GA, the first two signs in a break and restored by Langdon; an inscription has the name as Ti-ri-ga-an
